newsitem.title: USA: ATT team wins $5 billion U.S. military contract.
newsitem.headline: ATT team wins $5 billion U.S. military contract.

text.p: A team of companies led by American Telephone and Telegraph Co. has been awarded a $5 billion contract to provide new telecommunications equipment for the U.S. military, the Pentagon said on Wednesday.

The team, including a number of "Baby Bell" telephone companies around the United States as well as GTE and Time-Warner Communications, will install equipment at bases around the United States to carry secure voice, data and video communications around the world.

Senior Pentagon officials said 190 bids were solicited by the Defence Information Systems Agency and that only three bids were submitted. The two losing teams were headed by Sprint and MCI, officials said.

The contract, expected to run for nine years including eight one-year options, is the latest step in the American military's move to use commercial providers in upgrading to secure digital and other communications with state-of-the-art equipment.
Sites served by the equipment will include points ranging from the White House to soldiers in the field around the globe, according to defence officials.
